extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publishers, and open-science advocates interested in incentives and standards for data/materials sharing
extracted.subtask_description: Specifications and evaluative metrics for awarding journal 'open data' and 'open materials' badges, plus a coder rubric for assessing reported and actual availability, correctness, usability, and completeness of shared research data and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Data badge criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet the criteria to earn an open data badge, authors must make all digitally shareable data relevant to the publication available on an open access repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who meet the specification receive a badge and must provide an explicit statement in the paper including a URL to the data at an open repository. Independent repositories are preferred for preservation and quality assurance; 'upon request' or personal webpages are less desirable. Editorial checks can be used to validate compliance before awarding the badge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Materials badge criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To earn an open materials badge, authors must make all digitally shareable materials (e.g., survey items, stimulus materials, experiment programs) available on an open access repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials that cannot be shared digitally must be described in sufficient detail for an informed reader to know how to reproduce the protocol. As with data, authors must include an explicit statement and URL in the paper; independent repositories are preferred and editorial validation is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badge application and awarding process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors apply for badges upon article acceptance and provide evidence to editors that they met the specified criteria; awarded badges appear at the top of the paper and the paper includes an explicit repository URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badge implementation is low-cost and incremental; journals can choose to perform simple editorial checks on meeting criteria. Future improvements include embedding metadata in badges (a 'badge bakery') to record issuer, recipient, and resource location for programmatic discovery and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred sharing location (reported location)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting data or materials availability, indicate the location type: independent archive/repository, personal website, independent website, journal supplement, appendix or table, or 'available upon request'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent repositories are preferred because they provide stronger assurances of availability and preservation. 'Available upon request' is an ineffective policy because it occurs after publication and is often unfulfilled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability statement (presence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not the article makes a statement regarding the location, available or unavailable, of its data or materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit availability statement (including URL when applicable) is required for transparency and for badge eligibility; absence of a statement counts as not reporting availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reported available (claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not the article specifically states the data or materials were available for use, including noting that the data or materials are not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coding distinguishes between claiming availability and actually making resources accessible; reported availability is necessary but not sufficient for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actually available (retrievability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the data or materials reported available at a publicly accessible location were found at the expected location (excluding items embedded in article text, appendix, or journal-hosted supplement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coders attempted to retrieve resources at the reported URLs/locations; successful retrieval is required for this criterion. Editorial validation prior to badge issuance can ensure actual availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct data/materials (correspondence to description)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the data or materials could be retrieved, whether they corresponded to what was reported as being available (e.g., type of data, variables, participant counts, contents matching manuscript description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coders evaluated whether the retrieved items match the manuscript's description. For materials, coders checked that survey items, stimuli, or protocols matched the descriptions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usable data/materials (understandability and reusability)
rubrics_metrics.description: If data or materials could be retrieved, whether they were understandable and usable after brief review (format and context sufficient to allow reuse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coders assessed whether the format and contextual documentation made the resources likely to be usable for other researchers without extensive additional effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete data/materials (sufficiency for reproduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: If data or materials could be retrieved, whether all of the data or materials for reproducing the reported findings appeared to be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coders judged whether all data/materials described for all studies in the article were accessible. Coders did not necessarily reanalyze data; judgment was based on perceived sufficiency to reproduce reported results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding scheme uniformity (identical coding for data and materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of data and materials was coded using an identical coding structure with specified variables (e.g., badge awarded, availability statement, reported location, actually available, correct, usable, complete).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full coding scheme is publicly available and coders applied the same rules to both data and materials to enable consistent comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coder training and reliability standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Coders were trained to reliably apply the coding scheme and had to achieve 95% reliability with a gold-standard set before coding began; all questions including free-text answers were included in this reliability assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any coder response to the trial articles did not match the gold standard, it was marked incorrect and the coder repeated training with additional trial articles until reaching 95% agreement. This enforces consistent application of judgment-based metrics like 'usable' and 'complete'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion rules for retrieval checks
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing 'actually available' status, items embedded in the article text, appendix, or journal-hosted supplement were excluded from the retrieval-location check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The focus of the retrieval check was on publicly accessible external locations (repositories, personal/independent websites). Sharing that occurs only in-article or in journal supplements is treated differently in coding (counted as sharing but noted as often incomplete).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish reported vs. validated sharing (badge vs. no-badge nuance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether articles that report availability also earned a badge; compare rates of actual availability, correctness, usability, and completeness between articles with badges and without badges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical findings showed near-perfect availability and higher correctness/usable/complete rates for badge earners. This supports requiring validation steps prior to awarding badges to improve fidelity between reported and actual sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial validation and enforcement recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors or journal staff should perform simple procedures to validate data and material availability before issuing a badge and consider community guidelines for validation and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recommends implementing checks and considering provisions for situations where data/materials later disappear. Embedding metadata into badges can help monitoring and preservation. These practices help close gaps in badge specifications and improve adherence.
